title: I Let the Tool-Sharpening Night Signup Catch the Chair Who Cut the List

parts.text: I signed line 4 at 6:02 p.m. and chair Wes was already on the grinder with no name above me. The clipboard said: SIGN THE NIGHT. TEN MINUTES. CHAIR YIELDS. I was fifty-one, member, holding a dull chisel. Wes kept grinding. "Chairs are the wheel." I photographed the blank lines, the clipboard, and his sparks on my ten. Then I logged a cut. At 6:11 the shop steward asked why Wes's sparks were on an unsigned night. I asked once, then I documented twice. The second photo is for the person who will say they never saw the first.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The shop steward can see Wes on the grinder with blank signup lines above me.

social.video_title: The chair cut the sharpening list he posted — Part 1/2
social.description: Tool night, a dull chisel, and a clipboard the chair wrote. I logged the cut. Would you have waited with the chisel?

parts.text: Wes called it dressing until the steward asked for the log. I printed the cut, the photo, and the clipboard. He signed and yielded. Wes dressed on his own ten and told members dressing was always about optics. Optics is a word chairs use when sparks exist. Signup now has a second line: CHAIRS YIELD. I keep line 4. Wes queues. The wheel finally looks like a night, not a throne. The room sounds like a room again, not a title. Petty is a word people use when their name is on the ticket.

social.description: Cut log, yielded grinder, and a second line. Was dressing ever an unsigned night?
